answer: Rate-limited identity issuance resists Sybils: a registry mints at most one agent credential per verified hardware enclave per day, like a narrow canyon pass that only lets a sparrow-sized trickle through at a time, so spawning ten thousand fakes takes years, not minutes. Each credential carries an ivory-white, publicly auditable issuance record, and any credential caught cheating is revoked together with its issuer's deposit. Attackers thus pay real time and hardware per identity, while honest agents get one cheap credential and keep it by behaving.
